text:
Camila Reyes: Kicking off partner co-marketing thread for the regulated workloads webinar/roundtable. Partner wants to promote to their FinServ + Healthcare list next week.

We need to lock:
1) list building + who sends invites
2) partner logo approvals (landing page + deck)
3) lead sharing rules (esp. opt-in + GDPR)

@Noura El-Khoury can you propose dates/times + format? @Tyler Benson we’ll need a clear policy for lead sharing language on the form.

Noura El-Khoury: Yep. Option A: webinar (30 min content + 15 min Q&A), Option B: 45 min “roundtable” w/ moderated questions.

Partner suggested Thu 2/22 or Tue 2/27. If we want EMEA-friendly, 9am PT / 12pm ET / 5pm GMT works. If more NA, 11am PT.

My vote: Thu 2/22, 9am PT. Easier to get security folks.

Tyler Benson: On lead sharing: we need explicit checkbox language if we’re going to pass registrant details to partner.

We can do:
- default: consent to Redwood comms (required)
- optional: “Yes, share my info with <PartnerName> for follow-up” (unchecked by default)

If partner insists on full lead list regardless of opt-in, we should push back. Legal will not like it.

Soojin Lee: +1 pushback. Also we should clarify what “lead” means. Registrants != attendees. Partner keeps asking for “everyone who registers.”

We can share:
- opted-in registrants (fields: name, work email, company, title, country, consent timestamp)
- and separately attendee engagement (attended Y/N, questions asked) but only if opt-in covers it.

Markus Klein: From SE side: please don’t let partner commit us to “on-prem GA” or “HIPAA-ready out of the box” language. If co-branded assets go out, we need to keep it consistent with Security/GRC.

If we do “roundtable,” we should be explicit it’s architecture + checklist, not a product roadmap reveal.

Ethan Wallace: I can draft invite copy + landing page snippet today. Need partner’s exact brand name + how they want to be described (SI? marketplace partner? “implementation partner”?).

Also: do we want one landing page with both logos + two UTMs, or separate registration links per sender?

Ben Carter: Separate links per sender is easiest for attribution.

Plan:
- One landing page (co-branded)
- Two unique CTA links w/ UTMs:
  - redwoodinference.com/reg-webinar?utm_source=partner&utm_campaign=regulated_webinar&utm_medium=email
  - …utm_source=redwood

We can also set hidden field “partner_source=PartnerName” if they want deterministic tracking.

Grace O'Connor: For list building: I can have SDR team pull a “high intent” segment (CISO/GRC/platform eng at our ABM target accounts) and we’ll send a personalized version from the AE/SDR.

But we should avoid overlapping blasts w/ partner on the same day. Otherwise it looks spammy.

Suggestion:
- Partner sends Tues AM
- Redwood sends Wed AM
- Reminder from both the week prior (staggered)

Olga Petrov: Re: GRC perspective—if partner asks for SOC2 report to share broadly with registrants, that’s a no. We can provide the “security FAQ addendum” link and offer NDA path for evidence.

Also, landing page should not imply “BAA available by default” unless we’re sure. Use “BAA available on request for eligible customers” phrasing.

Camila Reyes: Great. I’m going to summarize partner asks from the last call:
- They want to use their logo on the landing page + in the deck
- They want “shared lead list within 24 hours”
- They want Redwood speaker + their compliance lead as co-host
- They want recording to send to no-shows

Action items:
@Ethan Wallace draft copy + proposed title
@Noura El-Khoury lock date/time + run-of-show
@Tyler Benson draft form consent language + lead sharing rules
@Soojin Lee sanity check claims/phrasing

Tyler Benson: Draft consent text for the registration form (feel free to tweak tone):

Checkbox A (required):
“I agree to receive communications from Redwood Inference related to this event and related products/services. I can unsubscribe at any time.”

Checkbox B (optional, unchecked):
“I agree that Redwood Inference may share my registration information with <PartnerName> so they can contact me about related services. <PartnerName> will use my information in accordance with their privacy policy.”

We should also add a link to partner privacy policy if possible.

Sofia Mendes: Jumping in—Tyler’s structure is the right approach.

Two legal notes:
1) Checkbox B must be opt-in (unchecked). No “by registering you agree…” language if we’re sharing.
2) If we’re doing EMEA, we should include country field and store the consent timestamp + language presented (for audit).

Also: if partner wants the recording, OK, but we must not include any customer names/logos in the demo unless we have permission.

Soojin Lee: Proposed title options (reg-safe):
1) “Deploying LLM Inference for Regulated Data: Private/VPC Patterns, Audit Logging, and Cost Controls”
2) “From Hosted to Private: Building Reliable LLM Inference for Financial Services & Healthcare”

I prefer #1. It’s less salesy and gets to the “how.”

Noura El-Khoury: Run-of-show (draft):
- 0–5 min: intros + who Redwood is + who partner is
- 5–20 min: “reference architecture” walkthrough (Private/VPC boundaries, KMS/HSM integration points, audit logging export patterns)
- 20–30 min: “security review fast-path” checklist (what to prepare, typical evidence)
- 30–40 min: Q&A
- 40–45 min: CTA (book security review / deep dive)

We’ll need a moderator. Camila or Soojin?

Camila Reyes: I can moderate. We should also keep it vertical-agnostic but with 1–2 examples per vertical.

Logo approvals: partner said they can approve within 48 hours if we send:
- placement mock (landing page header)
- deck cover slide
- email header usage

@Ethan Wallace can you include a quick “logo use request” email template to send to them?

Ethan Wallace: Yep. Also: we should ask them for their brand guidelines + approved lockups (light/dark) + min size rules.

Template:
“Hi <Name>, attached are proposed uses of your logo for our joint webinar. Please confirm approval for: (1) landing page header, (2) event promo email header, (3) webinar title slide + closing slide. If you have brand guidelines or preferred lockups, please share and we’ll align.”

Ben Carter: On landing page build: we can implement dual-UTM tracking + partner opt-in checkbox easily.

One more thing: do we want “co-registration” (partner uses their own registration form) or everything centralized on Redwood? Centralizing is cleaner for consent tracking.

My rec: centralize on Redwood landing page, give partner their own UTM link, and then share opted-in leads via weekly CSV.

Grace O'Connor: If we’re doing weekly CSV, can we commit to 24–48 hours post-event for the “hot leads” who request follow-up? Partner keeps emphasizing speed.

Maybe:
- Within 24 hours: send partner the opted-in list of “requested follow-up / meeting” (if we add a dropdown)
- Within 48 hours: send full opted-in registrant list

Tyler Benson: We can add a field:
“Are you interested in a Private/VPC architecture review?”
Options:
- Yes, contact me
- Not at this time

That gives us a clean “hot lead” subset to share fast.

Olga Petrov: Make sure that field doesn’t look like a compliance promise. Phrase it as “architecture review” / “security Q&A.”

Also, please route any “send me your SOC2” requests to the standard process.

Sofia Mendes: Agree. Also, if we share the “hot lead” subset within 24 hours, it must still be limited to those who checked the partner opt-in box. No opt-in = no share.

Camila Reyes: OK decision:
- Centralized Redwood landing page
- Two UTMs (Redwood + partner)
- Consent checkbox for partner (unchecked)
- Add “request architecture review” field
- Lead share:
  - within 24 hrs after event: opted-in + requested follow-up
  - within 48 hrs after event: all opted-in registrants + attendees flag (if covered)

Next: @Ben Carter @Tyler Benson can you confirm what fields we can share without causing issues (and what we should NOT share)?

Ben Carter: Safe share fields (if opt-in): first/last name, email, company, title, country, phone (if provided), interest flag, UTM source/campaign, consent timestamp.

Avoid: any behavioral tracking beyond “attended yes/no” unless explicitly disclosed. Also avoid sharing free-text questions unless we disclose “we may share questions with co-host.”

Tyler Benson: +1. We can add a small note under Q&A field: “Questions may be reviewed by event co-hosts to prepare responses.” But IMO we should keep it simple and not share questions.

Soojin Lee: One more messaging landmine: partner’s draft blurb says “Redwood supports data residency in any region and configurable retention from 0–7 years.” That’s not accurate.

We need to give them an “approved blurb” they must use. I’ll send a 2–3 sentence version.

Camila Reyes: Please do. Also can we set up a quick checklist before anything goes out? Like “PMM + Legal + GRC sign-off on co-marketing copy.”

Olga Petrov: Yes. Add me + Sofia on the final approval chain for the consent language and any security claims.

Noura El-Khoury: I’ll book a 20 min internal dry run next week once the deck is in shape.

Camila Reyes: Perfect. I’ll respond to partner today with:
- proposed date/time (Thu 2/22 9am PT)
- our lead sharing policy (opt-in only)
- request for brand guidelines + logos
- commitment to send “approved blurb” for invites

If they push back on opt-in: we escalate and likely walk away. This can’t jeopardize our compliance posture.

Sofia Mendes: +1. If they insist on full list, we should propose alternative: Redwood sends the follow-up on their behalf (“warm intro”) without sharing personal data. That’s often acceptable.

Camila Reyes: Good fallback. Will include that as option B.

Markus Klein: Also: if partner wants to present, let’s vet their slides. We can’t have them promising “HIPAA compliant inference” in the abstract.

Camila Reyes: Agreed. I’ll ask for their slide draft by end of next week.

Ben Carter: When you loop them in, please ask for their preferred logo filetype (SVG/PNG) + dark mode version. Designers always end up chasing this.

Camila Reyes: Noted. Thanks all. I’ll post partner response draft in this thread once sent for a quick :eyes: pass.
